data.description:
## Goal

Provide the agent framework with a shared, completion-aware wait helper so
agents stop burning sessions on fixed-length sleep polling of background jobs,
and give operators visible progress while a background process runs.

## Scope update (2026-10-18 reopen)

The helper core is **already delivered and committed to `dev`** (commit
`024194eb`): `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py`, 13 tests in
`skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py`, and a "Background job etiquette"
section in `skill/implement/SKILL.md`. A wiring audit then showed the helper
was referenced only by the implement skill; this item was reopened to roll
out the etiquette guidance and helper wiring across **all** skills and skill
scripts. The two children track that rollout:

- SA-0MVDP5JTK009HWOT — Roll out background-job etiquette guidance to all
  skills and global docs
- SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E — Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts where
  appropriate

The original scope ACs (core helper, tests, heartbeat, herdr reporting) were
satisfied by the delivered implementation; the open ACs below reflect the
reopened rollout scope. All original scope ACs are covered by the committed
helper and its tests.

## Justification (investigation findings)

Investigation of session `herdr-1792185693-133232-1304` (ran
`/skill:implement SA-0MSSSNOZN000LQKR`, an epic with 7 children):

- Session ran **23.7 hours** before intervention; it was still going when reviewed.
- **246 bash tool calls**, of which **95 were `sleep` calls totalling 21.0 hours —
  88.6% of the session was spent sleeping** (73 × `sleep 900`).
- **21 background processes** (`nohup`) were launched, each polled with the
  pattern `sleep 900; grep <log>; ps aux | grep` until completion.
- Pattern root cause: *fixed-length sleep polling is blind*. Each `sleep 900`
  is one turn — if the job finishes at minute 3 the agent still waits until
  minute 15 to discover it; if it stalls, the agent waits the full 15 minutes
  before deciding to retry. Every wake-up costs a full model round-trip
  (tokens, latency, context growth) and almost always returns "no change".
- Aggravating factors: heavy Local Proxy slot contention across ~12 concurrent
  herdr sessions made each audit take hours with repeated infra failures
  ("Connection error", "Script Execution Failure", stalls > 600 s, worklog lock
  contention), forcing re-launch/re-wait cycles.

## Out of scope

- The underlying Local Proxy slot-contention issue (separate infrastructure
  item) — better waiting cannot fix a serialised model slot.
- Fine-grained polling (`sleep 30`) as an alternative — that is *worse*
  (~2,400 round-trips over 20 h) and is explicitly an anti-pattern to avoid.

## Requirements (rollout scope)

1. **Shared/global documentation.** A canonical "background job etiquette"
   section in shared docs (referencing `wait_for_job.py`) that deprecates
   fixed `sleep N` polling of background processes, consistent with the
   implement skill section.
2. **Cross-skill rollout.** Every skill that launches or waits on background
   jobs (audit, ship, plan, test, …) and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` references the
   shared etiquette section at the relevant spots.
3. **Script wiring.** For each skill script that waits on a background
   subprocess/PR-status, record a decision (wire via `wait_for_job.py` or
   document "not appropriate"), and wire those marked appropriate so waits
   are completion-aware with timeout + heartbeat. Do not force integration
   where inappropriate.
4. **Behaviour parity.** Identical behaviour on environments without herdr env
   vars (helper silently degrades); existing tests still pass.
5. **Verification.** All tests pass via the test skill; docs and wiring
   committed and pushed to `dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A shared/global doc exists that documents the background-job etiquette
  pattern and explicitly deprecates fixed `sleep N` polling of background
  processes, referenced from the skills that launch or wait on background
  jobs (audit, ship, plan, test, AGENTS_GLOBAL).
- AC2: Every skill/location listed in the rollout references the shared
  etiquette section where it launches or waits on background jobs (e.g. audit
  SKILL.md, ship SKILL.md, plan SKILL.md, test SKILL.md, AGENTS_GLOBAL.md).
- AC3: No skill doc recommends a bare fixed-length `sleep N` polling loop for
  background processes.
- AC4: A per-candidate decision is recorded (wired / not appropriate, with
  reason) for each script that waits on a background job; every candidate
  marked wired invokes the shared helper (grep- or import-verifiable).
- AC5: The implement skill section and the shared section are consistent
  (same helper and pattern).
- AC6: All tests pass via the test skill; changes committed and pushed to
  `dev`; item advanced to `in_review` once the rollout children are complete.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQUQZMWB0067UCR** – PlanAll: claim command fails due to stage/status validation in wl (completed)
- **SA-0MQ8NQNAR009BM8Q** – Ralph Loop skill should stop once ralph loop started (completed)
- **SA-0MVCF4NKA00484JF** – Agent log review: global skill-improvement recommendations (2026-10-17 review) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+183 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0msssnozn000lqkr, absent, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+177 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+149 more)
data.title: Background-job wait helper with progress heartbeat (completion-aware waiting)

data.description:
## Goal

Wire the "background job etiquette" pattern (launch → prepare other work → one
completion-driven wait with progress → collect result) — delivered in
SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK with the shared helper `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` —
into **every** skill that agents actually run, not just the implement skill.
The parent item currently documents the helper only in
`skill/implement/SKILL.md`; agents running other skills still have no guidance
and may fall back to the deprecated fixed `sleep N` polling pattern.

## Background (wiring audit, SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK review)

`rg -l wait_for_job` across the repo matches only three files:
`skill/implement/SKILL.md`, `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py`, and
`skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py`. No other skill (audit, ship, plan,
test, refactor, cleanup, intake, interview, …) references the helper or the
etiquette pattern. `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, `command/`, and `docs/dev/` are
untouched — `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` still teaches the
`nohup python3 ./scripts/audit_runner.py … > "$LOG" 2>&1 &` launch pattern
with no completion-aware wait guidance, and the ship skill still waits on PR
status checks with a fixed 10-minute poll.

## Requirements

1. Add a canonical "background job etiquette" section to the shared docs
   (e.g. `skill/shared/` docs or `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`), referencing
   `wait_for_job.py` (SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK) and deprecating fixed `sleep N`
   polling of background processes.
2. Audit every skill's `SKILL.md`/docs/scripts for spots where agents launch
   or wait on long-running background jobs, and reference the shared etiquette
   section there. Minimum set identified by the wiring audit:
   - `skill/audit/SKILL.md` + `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (retry
     loops, nohup launch guidance)
   - `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (PR status-check wait)
   - `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/SKILL.md` (any background run
     guidance)
   - `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (global agent guidance)
3. Keep the implement skill's existing section consistent with the shared
   section (no divergence).

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A shared/global doc exists that documents the etiquette pattern and
  explicitly deprecates fixed `sleep N` polling, referenced from the skills
  listed in Requirement 2 (grep-verifiable).
- AC2: Every skill/location listed in Requirement 2 references the shared
  etiquette section where it launches or waits on background jobs —
  `rg wait_for_job` (or the shared section ref) matches each listed file
  (audit SKILL.md, audit-skill-reference.md, ship SKILL.md, plan SKILL.md,
  test SKILL.md, AGENTS_GLOBAL.md).
- AC3: No skill doc still *recommends* a bare fixed-length `sleep N` polling
  loop for background processes (grep-verifiable; intra-process retry sleeps
  in scripts are out of scope).
- AC4: The implement skill section and the shared section are consistent
  (both point at the same helper and pattern).
- AC5: All tests pass via the test skill; docs committed and pushed to `dev`;
  item advanced to `in_review`.


**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/` or `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — new canonical background-job etiquette section (referencing `wait_for_job.py`)
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — existing etiquette section to align with the shared section
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — reference etiquette at nohup launch/retry-loop guidance
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — reference etiquette at PR status-check wait
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/SKILL.md` — reference etiquette at any background-run guidance
- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — global agent guidance reference

**Dependencies:** SA-0MVDP9B83004UD5E (code wiring) — independent, can proceed in parallel; both must be complete before parent AC6 (in_review) is met.
data.title: Roll out background-job etiquette guidance to all skills and global docs

data.description:
## Goal

Explicitly wire the shared completion-aware wait helper `wait_for_job.py`
(SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK) into the **code/scripts that the skills execute** where
they launch or poll background processes, so the pattern is enforced
programmatically rather than relying solely on the model reading SKILL.md
prose. Parent-item wiring today is documentation-only: no skill script
imports or invokes `wait_for_job.py`.

## Background (wiring audit, SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK review)

`rg wait_for_job` matches only the helper, its tests, and the implement
SKILL.md prose. No script calls it. Candidates identified where a *script*
(rather than the agent model) waits on a long-running job:

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — background audit launches (nohup)
  and retry/queue-poll waits (`AUDIT_QUEUE_POLL_SECONDS`,
  `_PI_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS`); check whether wrapper scripts that launch
  audits in the background should wait via `wait_for_job.py`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/…` — PR status-check waits / merge waits.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `finish` test-run waits and any
  background subprocess waits.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — any
  subprocess completion waits.

## Requirements

1. **Investigate first**: for each candidate script, determine whether it
   waits on a background subprocess/PR-status and whether replacing/adding a
   `wait_for_job.py` invocation is appropriate (out of scope: intra-process
   lock/queue retry sleeps that are not background-job waits, and
   `wait_for_job.py` itself, which already exists).
2. Where appropriate, call `wait_for_job.py` (or import its helpers) so the
   script waits completion-aware with heartbeat rather than fixed sleep.
3. Do **not** force integration where it is not appropriate — document the
   decision per candidate in the work-item description/comments.
4. Keep behaviour identical on environments without herdr env vars (helper
   silently degrades).

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: A per-candidate decision is recorded (wired / not appropriate, with
  reason) for each script named in the Background section.
- AC2: Every candidate marked "wired" invokes the shared helper (grep- or
  import-verifiable) and its wait honours completion markers + timeout.
- AC3: Every candidate marked "not appropriate" has a documented reason, and
  no fixed-sleep polling of a *background job* remains in the wired paths.
- AC4: Existing tests for the touched scripts still pass ; new tests cover any
  new wait path (test skill).
- AC5: All tests pass via the test skill; changes committed and pushed to
  `dev`; item advanced to `in_review`.


**Key Files:**
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — background audit launches / queue-poll waits
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/` — PR status-check / merge waits
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — finish test-run waits
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — subprocess completion waits
- `skill/shared/wait_for_job.py` — the shared helper to wire in

**Dependencies:** SA-0MVDP5JTK009HWOT (docs rollout) — independent, can proceed in parallel; both must be complete before parent AC6 (in_review) is met.
data.title: Wire wait_for_job.py into skill scripts where appropriate
